message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the right or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I brought in some Scotch eggs to school, and my friend asked for a few, so I gave her some. We usually share food because sometimes only one of us has lunch. Then another friend came over and asked for one, and I agreed. Then, friend M walked over, dumped her bag on the table, and without saying a word, she lunged across the table to grab the eggs. I pulled them away and told her she couldn't have one. She asked why, and I said because she didn't ask nicely. Then another person did the same thing, lunging at my food without asking, and I didn't give them any either. Later, M apologized and asked nicely, but I told her she was only saying that because I told her to, and I didn't give her any eggs. I ended up eating the rest myself. Now, people are saying I'm the asshole for excluding her, but I was upset because she just grabbed without asking. I think the main issue here is about respect and how people ask for things. When someone just reaches out to take something without asking, it can feel rude. I was sharing with others who asked nicely, so I felt it was fair to exclude those who didn't. But maybe I was too harsh by not giving M any after she apologized. I wonder if it's okay to set boundaries about how people ask for things. On one hand, I was consistent by only giving to those who asked. On the other hand, maybe I should have given her one after she apologized, even if it was just to be nice. I also think about how others might see it. If I'm excluding someone who didn't follow the same rules as others, maybe it's justified. But if I'm too strict, it might come off as mean. In the end, I was just trying to share with people who were polite, but maybe I should have been more understanding, especially after she apologized. I'm not sure if I was in the right or not.
